articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Video, and 3D Assets
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring significantly improved long-context reasoning up to 1M tokens and native generation across text, image, audio, video, and 3D modalities within a single unified model. Benchmarks show substantial gains in complex multi-step coding tasks and scientific reasoning, with latency reduced by roughly 40% compared to the initial GPT-5 release earlier this year.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Graduate-Level Mathematics and Formal Verification
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on the FrontierMath and MathOlympiad benchmarks, solving over 80% of problems that previously stumped all frontier models. The model integrates a built-in formal proof assistant loop, allowing it to verify its own mathematical reasoning steps against Lean 4, dramatically reducing hallucinated proofs.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Supervised Deployment in Third-Party Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla has started deploying its third-generation Optimus humanoid robots in select Amazon and DHL warehouse facilities for supervised pick-and-pack operations. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22-DOF hands and on-device vision-language models enabling natural language task instruction, though they still require human oversight for edge cases.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C as Its Humanoid Robot Demonstrates Autonomous Retail Shelf Stocking
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a massive $1.5 billion Series C round at a $15 billion valuation after publicly demonstrating its Figure 02 robot autonomously stocking shelves at a pilot BMW retail parts facility. The robot leverages a transformer-based world model trained on thousands of hours of teleoperation data, enabling generalization to novel object geometries without retraining.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional Classifiers 2.0 to Defend Against Jailbreaks at the Infrastructure Level
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical paper and deployed Constitutional Classifiers 2.0 across its Claude model family, a layered defense system that reduces successful jailbreak rates to under 0.5% on adversarial benchmarks. The system uses lightweight classifier cascades trained via constitutional AI principles, operating at both the prompt and decoding stages with minimal latency overhead, addressing growing enterprise concerns about LLM security.

articles.title: ASML Reports Record EUV High-NA Orders as Intel and TSMC Race to Produce 1.4nm Node Chips
articles.summary: ASML disclosed record quarterly bookings for its next-generation High-NA EUV lithography systems, driven by aggressive orders from both Intel and TSMC targeting 14A and N1.4 process nodes respectively for 2027 production. The High-NA systems achieve 0.55 numerical aperture, enabling patterning of features below 8nm pitch, a critical enabler for continued transistor density scaling.

articles.title: Meta Open-Sources Llama 4 Behemoth, a 1.5-Trillion-Parameter MoE Model, Shifting the Open-Source AI Landscape
articles.summary: Meta released the full weights of Llama 4 Behemoth, a 1.5-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 128 experts, under a permissive license that now allows commercial use without revenue thresholds. Early community benchmarks place it competitive with proprietary frontier models on reasoning and coding tasks, further compressing the gap between open and closed-source AI capabilities and raising questions about safety governance.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance to Expand Brain-Computer Interface Trial to 50 Patients with Spinal Cord Injuries
articles.summary: The FDA granted Neuralink expanded approval to implant its N2 brain-computer interface device in up to 50 patients with cervical spinal cord injuries, following positive 12-month safety and efficacy data from its initial cohort. Participants demonstrated cursor control speeds approaching 60 bits per minute, with the latest firmware enabling direct control of robotic arm prosthetics in a research setting, marking a significant milestone for assistive neurotechnology.
